title: Windischgraetz brothers, Brussels, 18 Nov 1721 (DECODE R5029)

steps.what: Fetched DECODE R5029's five images, record page and attached xlsx with the project cookie.
Found Jakub Mirka's reconstructed key (2023) as the xlsx on the record itself; the catalogue's suggested keys R5017/R5018 are the Emperor's, not this cipher.
Transcribed the 13 cipher passages (181 groups) by eye from full-resolution crops, clear context in brackets (ct.txt).
Applied Mirka's two-numbers-per-letter table with dec.py: all letter-spelled passages give German (EXCUSATION ZU MACHEN, SUCCESSION, NIEMAHLEN ANZUNEHMEN).
Tried to fix open nomenclator codes (78, 103, 182, 205...) from context; none secure.
Fetched sibling records R5025-R5028 (16 images) with the project cookie.
Scanned all sibling cipher passages for interlinear glosses: 78=Compagnie, 103=Eugen (P.E./Eug.), 99=Engländer, 167=Graf Miosch confirmed; no gloss for the other 19 open codes.
Re-transcribed every cipher line of P2-P5 at full resolution; 4 vs 5 told apart by the c-hook on 5; p5 '9 45 18' corrected to '9 24 18' (GETHAN). All else confirmed.
Bracketed the 19 open codes in the alphabetical nomenclator against every context (182 nicht, 131 haben, 172 mit, 205 Rialp ...); proposals only, not counted as read.
New measure.py: letter runs checked word by word and LM-scored (de-1740s); codes counted only with listed or glossed values. 155/181 = 0.856.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R5029 linked to ct.txt (numbers with clear context) and dec.txt (dec.py output with Mírka's table, key.tsv)

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): dec.txt read: p2 and p3L build, but p3R-p4R have open codes, guesses and elided clear text in most clauses. R5029 relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read; method read with known key -> not solved; fraction_read 0.856 -> 0.

Re-read b37 step 1: DECODE R5029 record page re-checked (five images, the key xlsx, no transcription, comment or decipherment attachment); all five images opened at full resolution; P5 right and P1 are blank versos; the brown line-beginnings in the left margins of P3L-P5L belong to a larger sheet folded under the letter (not legible). Siblings R5025-R5028 already scanned 5 Oct. No print of a private brothers' letter found.

Transcribed the clear text of all five pages in full from full-resolution crops (R5029_transcription.txt); ct.txt context corrected: 'Casse(?)' = lasse, 'durchschnid' = durchgehends, 'Grentze' = [?Breunsche], 'Wartheimber' = Wertheimber (R5029_corrections.tsv); cipher labels unchanged.

Wrote the running German reading R5029_reading.md and translation R5029_en.md; two new sense-only code values from the alphabetical order: 101 [?eröffnen], 225 [?Wien]; the clear text identifies the writer as Ernst Friedrich (plenipotentiary at Cambrai, the Hague accession with Beretti Landi).

Scored the reading body: 0.615 clean sentences (32/52, de word list), 0.846 explicit holes only (b17_score.py HOLES=1); word-by-word alignment with the transcription (b37_align.py, R5029_align.txt): 18 unmatched words, all expansions of abbreviations or line-break joins. R5029 relabelled read (grade B).

outcome.method_basis: Jakub Mírka's reconstructed key (2023), attached to DECODE R5029, applied unchanged; four codes from interlinear glosses in the sibling letters R5025-R5028. The clear text was transcribed in full (23 Oct 2026) and the letter reads as a running German text; 19 nomenclator codes (26 groups) stay open or rest on sense only.

texts.label: R5029, Brussels, 18 Nov 1721
texts.summary: Ernst Friedrich von Windischgrätz, imperial plenipotentiary for the Congress of Cambrai, writes from Brussels to his brother at court in German with thirteen enciphered passages, deciphered with Jakub Mírka's key from the DECODE record: Prince Eugene is not well disposed to him and the Emperor advised against an excuse; everyone, even the Emperor, loses love for Eugene over the Ostend Company, the Prince's plan having lain unopened for two months; the English want to go home; the Spanish courier brought Pozobueno orders on the renunciations, so the Congress should open; he refuses a succession on a point of honour and asks to learn the Emperor's disposition towards him and his expenses.

reading_review.note: R5029_reading.md: the clear text transcribed in full from the five DECODE images (R5029_transcription.txt, 23 Oct 2026; before only excerpts), the cipher with Mírka's key and four sibling-glossed codes; 52 sentences, 0.615 clean on _check_reading (de word list), 0.846 counting explicit holes only (b17_score.py HOLES=1); the remaining breaks are open nomenclator codes ([205], [206], [168], [181], [204], [102], [151]) and sense-only code values marked [?word]. Word-by-word alignment: R5029_align.txt (no unbracketed word without a source). No look-alike pairs (numerical cipher). A reader can follow every sentence but two (the [168] ... [181] [206] clause and the [206] ... [?haben] clause).
